title: DFT Validation Dashboard
description: A pass/fail validation dashboard comparing computed DFT peaks against ground truth across a swept frequency range at an adjustable numerical tolerance.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Software Validation
DFT

educational.topic: Numerical validation of a DFT implementation
learningObjectives: Judge pass/fail against a stated numerical tolerance
Distinguish a resolution limit from an implementation bug
Propose a validation criterion that catches real defects

controls.label: Run full frequency sweep
controls.purpose: Evaluate every test case at the current tolerance

controls.label: Test frequency
controls.purpose: Step through the swept cases one at a time

equations: relative error = |peak bin frequency - f| / f * 100
assumptions: N = 64 at 16 kHz, bin spacing 250 Hz
Peak detection by simple maximum, with no interpolation
limitations: Peak-bin comparison cannot resolve better than half a bin; parabolic interpolation, covered in Chapter 15, would change these verdicts

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Evaluate against a standard, with a deliberately ambiguous failure pattern
keyQuestions: Do the failures correlate with bin alignment?
Would a real implementation bug fail differently?
commonMisconceptions: That any FAIL means the implementation is wrong
That loosening the tolerance until everything passes is a fix
assessmentOpportunities: Diagnose a uniform 2x magnitude error as a bug rather than a resolution limit
